# korean-word-of-the-day — a static Korean word-of-the-day resting screen

## What it is

`korean-word-of-the-day` is a static web page for a wall panel, tablet, or spare monitor. It shows one Korean word per day plus a Korean word clock that spells the current time the way Koreans say it. The repo contains two static files, `index.html` and `words.js`, with no build step, no API, no keys, no network calls, and no tracking. Opening `index.html` in any browser works, including with the internet down.

The word bank lives in a global `window.KOREAN_WORDS` array in `words.js`, with 20 entries total, from `설레다` to `편안하다`. Each entry has a `ko` field for Hangul (the hero glyph line), a `roman` field for Revised Romanization of the whole word, a `sound` field that is deliberately different from `roman` to show actual pronunciation, a `pos` field for part of speech, a `meaning` field for the definition line, a `syl` field with per-syllable `[hangul, roman]` pairs for the 'Syllables' block, and an `ex` field with `[korean, english]` example sentences for the 'In use' block.

Rotation of words is deterministic by local calendar date, with no API, tokens, or network. Index 0 is `설레다` so day one matches the approved mockup exactly. A specific date can pin a specific word.

The word clock is a letter grid that lights the current time as a spoken Korean phrase — native Korean numerals for hours, Sino-Korean for minutes, the way the time is actually said.

## Why it exists

The repo provides a resting screen for a wall panel, tablet, or spare monitor: one Korean word a day, plus a Korean word clock. It exists so a user can see a Korean word and its pronunciation without any setup or external dependency. Without it, the resting screen would have no content to display.

## How it is used

- **Owner:** opens `index.html` in any browser, or points a kiosk browser at the file (or the repo's GitHub Pages URL) at 1280×800 or similar.
- **Agent:** runs `node tests/test_korean_pin.js` for behavioral tests of the date-pin logic.
- **Automatic consumers:** none — the page makes no network calls and reads no external data.

## Boundaries

- **Owns:** the word bank (`words.js`), the date-pin rotation logic, the word clock rendering, and the static page (`index.html`).
- **Never does:** makes network calls or reads external data — the page is fully static and works offline; stores no user data or state — there is no persistence layer; renders media or images — the page is text-only.
- **Escalates to owner:** any change to the word bank shape or the date-pin logic, since the shape mirrors exactly what the Resting Screen design renders and adding a word is data-only, never a layout change.
- **Owner:** `UNKNOWN (fact not harvested)`.
